articles.title: Is it true that … toothpaste is an effective spot treatment?
articles.summary: It might dry out a pimple, but it could make things worse, so it’s worth exploring other solutions. The idea that toothpaste can be used to treat spots has been around for years. But does it actually work – or could it make things worse?
body: “A spot happens when a sebaceous gland gets plugged and inflamed,” says Dr Rosalind Simpson, a consultant dermatologist and associate professor at the University of Nottingham. Acne develops through a combination of blocked pores, increased sebum production and changes in Cutibacterium acnes, bacteria that naturally live on the skin.
The thinking is that ingredients such as baking soda or alcohol can dry out a pimple, making it appear smaller. But that doesn’t mean toothpaste is good for skin.

“One or two of the ingredients can temporarily dry out the skin a little bit,” says Simpson. “But the flipside is that other ingredients, such as menthol and sodium lauryl sulfate, are highly irritant to skin and could make the problem worse by increasing inflammation and worsening scarring and pigmentary change.”

She would not recommend treating a spot with toothpaste. Instead, she says, hydrocolloid acne patches can help reduce lesion size, redness and inflammation. Also, avoid picking or squeezing spots, which increases the risk of scarring; apply a warm cloth to the area; and use an over-the-counter topical treatment such as azelaic acid.
points: It might dry out a pimple, but it could make things worse, so it’s worth exploring other solutions.

articles.title: Ever Since I Knew Myself review – confronting the scars of childhood
articles.summary: Maka Gogaladze’s debut feature looks at generational differences in the context of Georgia’s education system and emphasis on collectivism. The scars imprinted on impressionable young minds can never fully fade away.
body: This debut feature would appear, at first glance, to be another act of revolt. Putting her mother in front of the camera, Gogaladze asks probing, at times blunt, questions about the strict education thrust on her in childhood. Together, they talk about piano lessons that ended in tears, and tough academic exams that continued to haunt the director well into her adulthood. Their contrasting personalities are fascinatingly revealed across these conversations in all their tension, yet these sequences also represent a moving effort to reach across generational differences.

Gogaladze widens the frame to include a series of observational vignettes shot at various children’s classes in Georgia. The subjects vary – history lessons are sandwiched between ballet and dance sessions – yet the disciplined atmosphere remains the same. Even during art class, teachers leave little room for individual expression or debate. Obedience, rather than dialogue, is the order of the day.
points: Maka Gogaladze’s debut feature looks at generational differences in the context of Georgia’s education system and emphasis on collectivism.

articles.title: ‘Meet my new après buddies!’: a joyous group skiing trip in Les Deux Alpes, France
articles.summary: One large ski chalet in the French Alps and 17 strangers. An organised trip for solo travellers is a leap into the unknown. Everyone had their reasons for joining the trip.
body: I was there because I needed a ski gang. None of my friends ski, and my brother was out of action with an injury. Not only that, I needed a good night’s sleep. I love my two-year-old son dearly, but I have somehow spawned an insomniac – still waking four times a night. Weary from bedtime battles, Holly, my partner, bluntly pointed out we could both benefit from “a temporary break from family life”. In other words: separate holidays.

Holly arranged a walking trip with friends; I opted for a week’s skiing in the French ski resort of Les Deux Alpes with Friendship Travel, a specialist operator in solo travel for more than 20 years. They find a chalet, fill it with solo skiers, provide travel, most meals and group ski lessons – that’s the basic service.

articles.title: The one change that worked: I told the men in my life I loved them – and my world opened up
articles.summary: At first I felt uncomfortable telling my dad, brother and friends how I felt. But I soon found it liberating, and once I started, I couldn’t stop. Until my thirties, I didn’t tell my brothers or my dad that I loved them. I had never told my friends, whom I love, that I loved them.
body: Then, in 2023, I made the mistake of reading books on masculinity. It started with JJ Bola, Ivan Jablonka, Rebecca Solnit and RW Connell, then I got carried away with Simone de Beauvoir, Judith Butler and Audre Lorde. But one book performed a small act of sorcery: it made me question my life. The Will to Change by bell hooks felt revolutionary, full of generosity towards men, particularly tough men or men who performed toughness. It spoke of the need for us to break barriers and practise intimacy. “It is not true that men are unwilling to change,” hooks writes. “It is true that many men are afraid to change.”

So I decided to change. It might seem like a small change, but to me it felt terrifying: I’d start telling the men I love that I loved them. I started as soon as I’d finished the book. I felt so uncomfortable on the first few attempts that it activated my autonomic nervous system, triggering a fight-or-flight response. “I love you,” I declared to one of my best mates, near the barriers of Shepherd’s Bush tube station, then I ran inside and never looked back.
points: At first I felt uncomfortable telling my dad, brother and friends how I felt.
Until my thirties, I didn’t tell my brothers or my dad that I loved them.
I had never told my friends, whom I love, that I loved them.
Then, in 2023, I made the mistake of reading books on masculinity.

articles.title: How Vestiaire Collective Is Keeping Stolen Goods From Being Resold
articles.summary: Following reports of recently looted goods appearing on resale platforms, the luxury marketplace is stepping up scrutiny of suspicious listings.
body: At luxury resale platform Vestiaire Collective’s largest authentication warehouse, situated in an old spinning mill in Torcoing, northern France, the scale and rigor of their operation becomes apparent. Security personnel escort guests through the metal gates and into the discreet red brick building where they must place their bags in lockers before proceeding further. The factory floor is bustling with workers in white Vestiaire Collective lab coats, unpacking items as they arrive by conveyor belt, authenticating them, checking their condition and packaging them up again to send to sellers across the world.

Vestiaire Collective has always taken a multi-step approach to authenticating luxury goods to prevent counterfeits and fraud. But now it faces a new challenge. Shortly after the lootings that took place across France and Italy from October 17, reports emerged of stolen goods appearing on popular resale platforms. Luxury brands including Louis Vuitton, Dior, Celine, and Hermès are some of the most sought-after labels on Vestiaire. Now, the marketplace is taking measures to avoid reselling stolen goods from Milan and Paris shop floors.

articles.title: Fashion Is Betting on Spooky Season
articles.summary: With Halloween spending strong, fashion is tapping into a fresh appetite for spooky looks that last beyond October 31. What’s working?
body: Spooky Season is fast approaching, but the most hardened Halloween fashionistas have been ready for months. While the broader category of costume shoppers will err toward value, a strong luxury and style-led contingent are investing in forever pieces, looking to rare vintage numbers and one-off statement designs to anchor their Halloween look. The caveat? They can wear these items repeatedly throughout the year.

Halloween is big business. According to the National Retail Federation (NRF), 71% of US consumers plan to purchase costumes this year, generating an estimated $4.4 billion across age groups. Per Deloitte’s 2026 Halloween survey, 92% of US households are looking to participate in the holiday this year. The report found that households intended to spend an average of $219 across retail categories, with 56% of shoppers planning to complete their first purchase before October.
points: With Halloween spending strong, fashion is tapping into a fresh appetite for spooky looks that last beyond October 31.

articles.title: 11 Foods To Increase Your Ferritin Levels
articles.summary: The best foods to help increase your ferritin levels are foods that are rich in iron. Here, the experts break down everything you need to know.
body: If you’ve been diagnosed with iron deficiency by a medical professional, you’re probably familiar with ferritin. But even then, though the two are connected, they aren’t interchangeable, as many are led to believe. “Ferritin is different [than iron that most people are familiar with],” integrative nutritionist and psychologist Karishma Shah tells Vogue. “It is your storage form of iron.”

“Think of it as your iron savings account,” adds Real Nutrition founder Amy Shapiro, RD. “When a doctor measures serum ferritin, they're getting a snapshot of how much iron you have in reserve. Low ferritin is often the first sign that iron stores are running low, sometimes long before anemia shows up. That's why people can feel tired, foggy, cold, or notice hair shedding even when their hemoglobin looks normal.”
So what’s the fix? Should you find that you may be dealing with an iron deficiency, one of the easiest ways to treat it is through your diet.
points: The best foods to help increase your ferritin levels are foods that are rich in iron.

articles.title: How ‘La Bola Negra’’s Costume and Production Designers Crafted Its Sensuous Universe
articles.summary: “La Bola Negra” is Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s most ambitious work to date. So, too, is it a major achievement for their collaborators Ana Cobos and Roger Bellés.
body: After nearly a decade of making visionary, queer-centric work, Spanish filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, known together as Los Javis, have reached dizzying new heights with La Bola Negra, inspired by the life and work of Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca.

The film centers on Sebastián (singer Guitarricadelafuente), Carlos (Milo Quifes), and Alberto (Carlos González)—three gay men living in 1932, 1937, and 2017, respectively—who are connected by one of Lorca’s unfinished plays, La Bola Negra. Blending historical narrative, fiction, and fantasy as it explores how shame and resilience can be a kind of inheritance, the hyper-stylized epic is Calvo and Ambrossi’s most ambitious work to date. So, too, is it a major achievement for Los Javis’ collaborators Ana Cobos, La Bola Negra ’s costume designer, and Roger Bellés, who headed production design.

articles.title: Where to Stay When Visiting Alaska's Denali National Park
articles.summary: The best hotels, lodges, and cabins for a trip to the Last Frontier.
body: With broad river valleys, colorful meadows peppered with fireweed and lupine, forests thick with spruce and aspen, and the snow-covered Alaska Range rising in the distance, Denali National Park and Preserve is one of those places that can still feel startlingly wild no matter how many times you visit. At 6.1 million acres, it’s larger than Massachusetts, and the sheer scale of the national park means a trip here can look very different depending on where you choose to stay.

I’ve selected the best stays across that spectrum, from full-service hotels and family-friendly cabins to secluded backcountry lodges and even a chalet set on a glacier just miles from the summit of North America’s highest peak. Read on for my favorite places to stay near Denali National Park in Alaska.
